# Scoping and Shadowing

> **Gap** GAP-DECLARATIONS-004

Variables are [lexically scoped](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-1). Each block `{ }` introduces a new scope. Inner scopes can shadow outer variables.

`let` and `var` declarations are [sequential](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-2) — a binding is visible only from its declaration point to the end of its containing block.

`fun` declarations are [hoisted to the top of their containing block](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-3). All `fun` declarations in a block are mutually visible to each other and to all other statements in that block, regardless of declaration order. This enables forward references and mutual recursion at any nesting level.

Hoisting is block-local: a `fun` declared in an inner block is not visible in the outer block. Normal lexical scoping applies across block boundaries — inner blocks see outer declarations, outer blocks do not see inner declarations. The body of a local `fun` is the exception: it does not see the locals of the enclosing function, only items ([Functions — Local Functions](../../functions/declarations.md#local-functions)).

```metel
fun is_even(n: i64) -> boolean {
    if (n == 0) { return true; }
    return is_odd(n - 1);
}

fun is_odd(n: i64) -> boolean {
    if (n == 0) { return false; }
    return is_even(n - 1);
}

fun outer() -> i64 {
    inner();

    fun inner() {
        helper();
        fun helper() { }
    }

    return 1;
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    if (is_odd(3)) { return outer(); }
    return 0;
}
```

An inner function [remains scoped to its own block](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-3). For example, `helper();` is valid inside `inner()`, but calling `helper();` from `outer()` is a type error.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="demonstrates that helper() is not visible from outer() -- the type error is the point" -->
```metel
fun outer() {
    fun inner() {
        fun helper() { }
        helper();
    }

    helper();
}

fun main() {
    outer();
}
```

[A module's top-level names live in two namespaces](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-5). Structs, enums, aspects and type aliases
share the type namespace; functions, `let` and `var` share the value namespace. Declaring a
name twice in one namespace is an error ([T0037](../../../error-codes.md#t0037--duplicate-top-level-declaration));
a type and a value may share a name, and two functions of one name form an overload set.

Top-level `struct` and `enum` declarations are [hoisted to program scope](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-4) — they may be
referenced before their declaration appears in the source.

Types declared inside a function body are local to that body from their declaration
point onward; they are not visible from other functions. A local `struct`, `record` or `enum`
may declare type parameters and bounds exactly as a top-level one does (`record Box<T> { x: T }`);
they are checked where the type is constructed and applied at each use.

```metel
fun make_point() -> Point {
    return Point { x = 1.0, y = 2.0 };   // OK — Point is globally visible
}

struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

fun inner() {
    struct LocalPoint {
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    }
    let p := LocalPoint { x = 1.0, y = 2.0 };
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    inner();
    let p := make_point();
    return p.x as i64;
}
```

Top-level `extend` blocks follow the same declaration-order rule as the types they extend.

<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-1}

Each block introduces a lexical scope. A declaration in an inner scope may shadow an outer
declaration, and the outer declaration is not visible outside its own scope.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-2}

A `let` or `var` binding is in scope from its declaration through the end of its containing
block, but not before its declaration.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed e7d2c1d4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-3}

Function declarations are visible throughout their containing block regardless of source
order, including to other functions in that block; this hoisting does not extend out of an
inner block.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-4}

Top-level struct and enum declarations are visible throughout the program regardless of
source order. A type declared inside a block is visible only from its declaration to the end
of that block.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-5}

A module's top-level names live in two namespaces, for lookup: the *type* namespace holds
structs, enums, aspects and type aliases; the *value* namespace holds functions, `let` and
`var`. A name declared twice in one module, in either namespace, is rejected with
[`T0037`](../../../error-codes.md#t0037--duplicate-top-level-declaration) — a type and a value
of one name conflict exactly as two types or two values of one name do. Two functions of one
name are an overload set instead (identical parameter types are rejected as `T0011`), and
`let _ := ...` binds no name, so it may be repeated.

<!-- rfc.py:exemption kind="blocked" ref="metel-core#2198" reason="A type and a same-named value still coexist today; the duplicate-declaration check (name_resolver::check_duplicate_declarations) still runs within one namespace only, not across both." -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-6}

A type and a value of one name may not coexist in a module (`struct Foo` beside `fun Foo`
is a duplicate declaration, [legality-5](#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-5)).
A type position always resolves in the type namespace: a type annotation, an `extend` or
aspect target, the head of a struct, record or enum literal, and the head of a pattern.

<!-- rfc.py:exemption kind="blocked" ref="metel-core#2198" reason="A type and a same-named function still coexist today, so this rule's premise -- that a type position never needs to choose between competing declarations -- does not yet hold generally; it holds today only because the compiler does not yet forbid the coexistence legality-5 now also covers." -->

<!-- rfc.py:exemption:rendered:start -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-7}

A bare name in expression position resolves in the value namespace, and, when the module has
no value of that name, in the type namespace (a zero-field struct used as a value). A local
binding of the same name shadows both: the name then refers to the local for the rest of its
scope, and a call through it calls the local.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-8}

The names of the intrinsic types (`boolean`, `String`, `Char`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `u8`,
`u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `f32`, `f64`, `Range` and `RangeInclusive`) are reserved in the type
namespace: declaring a struct, enum, aspect, type alias or block-local struct or enum with one of
them is rejected with [`T0038`](../../../error-codes.md#t0038--declaring-a-type-with-the-name-of-an-intrinsic-type).
A function or `let` may use the name, and the rule does not cover the types `std::core`
declares (`List`, `Option`, `Result`, ...).

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-9}

A module may declare a type with the name of one `std::core` declares (`Option`, `Result`,
`List`, ...), and the module's own declaration then wins for every name written in that module. A
value that std produced keeps the type std declared: a `match` on it names the variants of that
type, and a method called on it is found on that type, whichever type the name now means in the
caller.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 052e8604c616372659749277ef96efec80d79fe6 -->
